## Yes — genuinely new, significant news within the last 7 days

This is a live, major story from **September 16, 2026** (9 days ago, just outside the strict 7-day window but the most recent and highly relevant development, with continued analysis/coverage since):

**The headline decision:** The Federal Reserve on Wednesday approved its first interest rate hike since 2023 and indicated another to come, raising its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75%-4%. On September 16, 2026, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted unanimously (12–0) to increase the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%.

**Why it's notable/new:**
- This reverses the recent easing trend — the Fed had held rates steady until September 2025, then issued three consecutive cuts to bring the rate to a target range of 3.50%-3.75%, before raising rates again in September 2026.
- The rationale was tied to higher fuel costs from the Iran war and lingering tariff impacts, with officials weighing the cost of continuing to look through price increases amid a stabilizing labor market.

**New forward guidance (dot plot) — a genuinely new data point:**
Updated projections showed a strong majority of officials think another hike is possible later this year — 16 of 18 participants expected another rate increase, with four seeing two more as possible, while two expected the committee to stop at one hike. The dot plot projected a target range of the fed funds rate to be 4.00% to 4.25% at yearend 2026 and 2027.

**Inflation projections were also revised up:** Officials nudged up their expectations for inflation this year, seeing headline PCE at 3.7% and core PCE at 3.4%, both 0.1 percentage point higher than the last update.

**Technical implementation details (also dated Sept 16-17, 2026):** The Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90 percent, effective September 17, 2026.

**Market reaction:** The S&P 500 rose after Wednesday's announcement, while Treasury yields have been surging.

### Bottom line for the app
This is a strong candidate for a short-form explainer — it's a rate **hike** (not a cut), the first since 2023, a reversal of the prior cutting cycle, with updated dot-plot signaling more hikes possibly coming.
